title: Consumer project record
description: Schema for a consuming project's .ci/project.yml, per docs/gitlab-ci-agent-standard.md section 4. The record says which shared composition a project adopted, under which instance names, what it kept bespoke and what it retired. It is metadata, not GitLab configuration: nothing reads it at pipeline time, and every value it names must also be resolved into the committed .gitlab-ci.yml. See docs/reference/project-yml.md.

reason.description: Why, in a sentence a reviewer who was not there can act on. Not a label.

instance.description: Component instance, the first half of every job name it creates.

inputValue.description: A scalar, a list of scalars, or a list of flat mappings — the last being the needs-entry shape a gate-jobs input takes.

project.description: The consuming project's own GitLab path, group included.

shared_ci.description: Which shared-CI project and revision the committed pipeline pins. The ref must be the value in the .gitlab-ci.yml, not an intention.

ref.description: Full commit SHA, protected release tag, or REPLACE_WITH_APPROVED_SHARED_CI_REF in an example. A branch name is not a ref this standard accepts (section 14.2).

workload.description: What this project is, in the vocabulary of pipelines/<workload>.yml.

name.description: A composition name when one fits, otherwise the shape of the work: python-tests, docs-site, artifact-mirror, machine-image.

adoption.description: composition: the project includes a shared composition. bespoke: the project keeps its own pipeline because no composition fits. held: adoption is blocked on a decision, which the reason names.

then.description: Anything other than a plain adoption is a decision, and a decision without its reason cannot be reviewed.

compositions.description: Every shared composition this project includes, in include order. Empty for a bespoke or held workload.

file.description: The composition path as the include writes it, for example /pipelines/container-buildkit.yml.

instances.description: Every component instance this include names, in the order its inputs declare them. One for most compositions; repository-secret-audit names two in one include.

inputs.description: The inputs the include sets explicitly, copied as written. Defaults are not restated: what is recorded is what the project chose.

bespoke_jobs.description: Jobs the project still defines itself beside the composition, each with the reason no component covers it.

retired_jobs.description: Jobs the adoption removed. A job that disappeared without a line here is a job nobody decided to lose.

environments.description: Deployment targets this project acts on, where it has any. state_id is the Terraform state name, target the cluster, registry project or host the environment resolves to.

exceptions.description: Identifiers of recorded exceptions this project relies on, resolved in .ci/exceptions.yml. Ids only: the exception itself, its owner and its expiry live there.

notes.description: Anything a reviewer needs that no field above holds. Prose, not a second schema.
